synopsis: Volvo CE's Collision Mitigation System launched in January 2023, with a press release dated 11 January; the original wheel-loader system operated only in reverse at 3–15 km/h [f1065, f10625, f1382]. It requires Radar Detect and applies the service brakes for 2–3 seconds before the operator takes over; it is explicitly not intended to replace safe operator behaviour [f1383, f1625, f1630]. The original factory-fit offering covered specified loader models, including L110H and L120H with OptiShift, rather than an unrestricted machine family; Volvo says these loaders spend 40–50% of their time reversing [f10629, f10438, f10630]. Slope memory avoids activation when reversing down stockpiles, and the system can be temporarily deactivated for particular site conditions [f1384, f10631, f10632]. A new generation was announced in April 2025, with reverse obstacle alerts from 0.5 km/h and additional named loader models, but the announcement does not establish whether the automatic-braking speed band changed [f1623, f1386, f1624, f1387]. Development and validation were in-house with internal evidence acceptance, but published validation methods, development and validation durations, remaining physical testing, environmental limits, false-positive rates and minimum object size were unavailable, limiting its usefulness as a validation-planning benchmark [f1379, f1860, f1862, f1066, f1388, f1861, f1631].
